verdict_reason: This PR only rewrites the package declaration (rename address.book -> addressbook), but the body it carries over is never invoked - '@EnableScheduling' is absent from the whole repo so the EMF publisher is dead code - and it also drops meter tags/statistics, aborts the whole cycle on a NaN gauge, and destructively mutates the shared MeterRegistry; namespace and dimension cardinality are fine (no per-organisation or per-address dimension) and there is no thread-safety or request-path risk since MetricsLogger is per-invocation on a scheduler thread

todos.issue: publishMetrics() never runs: '@EnableScheduling' appears nowhere in the repo (grep across all of src returns nothing) and no production code calls publishMetrics() - only tests do - so Spring never registers a ScheduledAnnotationBeanPostProcessor and the whole EMF publication path is dead code despite the aws.emf.* config and CDP CloudWatch endpoint being wired up
todos.fix: Add '@EnableScheduling' to Application (or a SchedulingConfig '@Configuration' class as per spring-boot.md section 11) and back it with an integration test that asserts the scheduled task is actually registered, not just that the annotation is present

todos.issue: Every measurement is published under the bare meter name - both Meter.Id tags and Measurement.getStatistic() are discarded - so a Timer's COUNT, TOTAL_TIME and MAX all collapse into one metric key, and the ~8 differently-tagged jvm.memory.used meters (area x pool) merge into a single unusable series; unit is also lost (defaults to Unit.NONE) even though timers are in nanoseconds
todos.fix: Qualify the EMF key with the statistic (e.g. name + '.' + measurement.getStatistic().getTagValueRepresentation()), pass the correct Unit, and emit the meter's low-cardinality tags as EMF dimensions via putDimensions(DimensionSet) so series stay distinguishable

todos.issue: putMetric() is called with no guard: aws-embedded-metrics 4.2.0 Validator.validateMetric throws the unchecked InvalidMetricException when !Double.isFinite(value), and Micrometer gauges legitimately report NaN (e.g. a gauge whose weak reference has been collected), so one NaN aborts the forEach before flush() at line 47 and silently drops every metric for that cycle - recurring every 60s while the bad meter exists
todos.fix: Skip non-finite measurements (if (!Double.isFinite(value)) return;) and wrap the publish body in try/catch logging at WARN so metric publication is best-effort and flush() still runs; add a unit test covering a NaN gauge

todos.issue: The publisher destructively mutates the shared application MeterRegistry every 60s, removing every meter whose name startsWith the undocumented magic string 'controller' - this wipes those series from the exposed actuator /metrics endpoint and leaves mixed semantics, since controller.* is published as a per-minute delta while all other meters (jvm.*, http.server.requests.active) are published as cumulative totals
todos.fix: Drop the removal and let CloudWatch derive rates from cumulative counters, or publish into a dedicated per-window registry that is not the shared bean; if the reset must stay, extract the prefix to a named constant and document the delta-vs-cumulative split. Also reuse the single getMeters() result instead of calling it twice

todos.issue: MetricsLogger is constructed inline inside publishMetrics(), so nothing published to EMF can be asserted - EmfMetricsPublisherTest can only verify(meterRegistry, times(2)).getMeters(), which asserts implementation detail rather than any published namespace, metric name or value
todos.fix: Inject a Supplier<MetricsLogger> (or a thin MetricsLoggerFactory bean) so tests can capture the logger and assert the namespace, metric keys and values actually emitted

todos.issue: The bean is gated on management.metrics.enabled, but application.yml defines a dedicated aws.emf.enabled flag (line 42) that no code reads - so EMF publication cannot be switched off independently of Micrometer, and the dedicated flag is dead configuration
todos.fix: Gate on the purpose-built flag: '@ConditionalOnProperty(name = "aws.emf.enabled", havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = false)', and update MetricsConfigurationPropertiesTest accordingly - or delete aws.emf.enabled from application.yml if the coarser gate is intended

todos.issue: Unused imports carried into the renamed package: io.micrometer.core.instrument.composite.CompositeMeterRegistry (line 4) and java.util.List (line 5) are never referenced (Sonar java:S1128)
